englishBlockReviews.reason: Engineering-property overview and equation (2-19) reference are retained. The ideal-gas applicability qualification is translated without upgrading it to a universal real-gas claim.

The pressure formula has mol*(J/mol/K)*K/m^3=Pa units. Separate formal limits and the low-temperature/model warning remain. F=pS denotes the force on the receiving wall surface under uniform pressure, not a resultant force on the whole closed vessel. The spring analogy remains qualified and non-Hookean.

Mass proportionality retains fixed gas species, volume and temperature. Tire/soccer-ball inflation, releasing gas, safe operating limits, compression pumps and the qualified piston-water-pump comparison are all present.

Ordinary gas compressibility is not made universal. Independently, for an isotherm p=A/V and volume reduction d with A>0 and 0<d<V, the increase A*d/[V*(V-d)] is larger at smaller initial V. V1/V2, Delta V and Delta p1/Delta p2 are not reversed. Expansion and compression work directions and the conditions for small pressure variation remain.

Fig-26 identity and caption number remain; pixels are not assessed. Purpose-built pressure-vessel storage/transport and permitted pressure/temperature conditions match the retained Chinese, without turning an ordinary bottle into a rated vessel.

Fixed-amount heating at fixed volume and fixed pressure are distinguished. The source textbook's Charles/Gay-Lussac naming is explicitly source-attributed, not presented as an unqualified modern naming convention. The inverse-temperature coefficient 1/273 uses the Celsius-zero reference and source approximation; the several-hundred-times comparison remains attributed and material/range-qualified.
Small gas mass producing appreciable pressure is conditioned on volume and temperature. Rarefied molecular arrangement and momentum exchange at the walls preserve the concluding topic.
